chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I asked him about various types of different clothes which the person in Ihram wears when he needs them. What is upon him? He said: For every type from it, there is an expiation.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.فِدَاء: Expiation or compensation offered for a specific act or omission

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for wearing different types of clothes while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of proportional expiation (fidyah) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between distinct categories of garments rather than imposing a single penalty for all. It reflects the scholarly consensus that necessity (darurah) permits wearing sewn clothes, but requires compensation for each specific type worn, ensuring the ritual purity of the Ihram state is maintained through tangible restitution. This ruling underscores the balance between ease in ritual observance and strict adherence to the sanctity of the pilgrimage rites.
